newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares end up, U.S. to set Friday's agenda.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares end up, U.S. to set Friday's agenda.

text.p: Danish share prices closed higher in a quiet market on Thursday despite bond declines with dealers foreseeing that Wall Street overnight trends would determine the way trading shaped up to the weekend break.

"The Danish stock market was mainly pulled op by Germany this afternoon after an eventless morning. We expect low activity again tomorrow, indeed it could be quiet for the rest of the year," one dealer said.
The KFX top-20 index ended the day 0.59 point up at 131.74, while the KFX December future rose 0.90 point to 131.60 with 488 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
SAS was the most traded share of the day, with some 388,000 shares traded, but it closed unchanged at 72.
ISS was also in focus with 151,000 shares traded, ending two crowns higher at 164, while Tele Danmark rose by the same amount to 298.
